Prompt-tuning has emerged as a parameter-efficient technique for adapting large-scale vision-language models (VLMs) to downstream tasks while keeping the pre-trained weights frozen. However, prompt-tuned VLMs often suffer from a base-to-novel dual miscalibration problem, where models typically show underconfidence on base classes and overconfidence on novel classes. Current VLM calibration...

WHY IT MATTERS

M-PFT introduces a geometric angular-margin approach to solve the base-to-novel miscalibration problem in prompt-tuned vision-language models, offering a sound technical contribution to parameter-efficient tuning.
